record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable points on manifolds
record.original_question: Using dynamics, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable vectors lying in a nondegenerate submanifold of R^n?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 36 (D. Kleinbock). Give estimates of the Hausdorff dimension of v - approximable vectors in a nondegenerate submanifold of Rn using dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers n ≥ 2 and d with 1 ≤ d < n. A smooth submanifold M ⊂ ℝⁿ of dimension d is called nondegenerate at a point x ∈ M if, in some (equivalently any) smooth parameterization f: U → M with f(u₀) = x (U ⊂ ℝᵈ open), the partial derivatives of f of order up to some finite k span ℝⁿ. The manifold M is called nondegenerate if it is nondegenerate at almost every point.

Let v = (v₁, …, vₙ) be an n-tuple of positive real numbers with v₁ + ⋯ + vₙ = 1. A vector y = (y₁, …, yₙ) ∈ ℝⁿ is called v-approximable if there exist infinitely many q ∈ ℕ such that
    max₁≤i≤n ‖qyᵢ‖^{1/vᵢ} < 1/q,
where ‖·‖ denotes the distance to the nearest integer. Denote by W(v) the set of v-approximable vectors in ℝⁿ.

Develop a method, based on the dynamics of one-parameter diagonal flows on the homogeneous space SL_{n+1}(ℝ)/SL_{n+1}(ℤ) and the correspondence between Diophantine approximation and excursions of lattice orbits into the cusp, that yields estimates (upper and/or lower bounds) for the Hausdorff dimension of W(v) ∩ M for an arbitrary nondegenerate submanifold M of ℝⁿ.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made via dynamics and other techniques: Beresnevich (2017) and Beresnevich–Vaughan–Velani–Yang established lower bounds for Hausdorff dimension of (weighted) approximable points on nondegenerate manifolds; complementary upper-bound results exist for curves and analytic manifolds. However, sharp two-sided dimension estimates for v-approximable vectors on general nondegenerate submanifolds, obtained purely via dynamics, remain incomplete, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Diophantine Approximation on Manifolds and Lower Bounds for Hausdorff Dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Beresnevich establishes lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of sets of approximable points on nondegenerate manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds for Hausdorff dimension of approximable points on nondegenerate submanifolds have been established.

status_evidence.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of sets of well-approximable points on nondegenerate curves
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Hausdorff dimension for well-approximable points on nondegenerate curves.
status_evidence.claim: Dimension estimates exist for the curve case (d=1).

status_evidence.title: On Fractal Measures and Diophantine Approximation (Kleinbock-Lindenstrauss-Weiss)
status_evidence.snippet: Uses dynamics on homogeneous spaces and friendly measures to study Diophantine approximation on nondegenerate submanifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Dynamics-based methods have been developed for these problems but do not yet yield sharp dimension formulas in full generality.
